Law: The Constitution of Pakistan, 1973: Article 25-A guarantees the right to free and compulsory education for all children aged 5 to 16 years, making it a fundamental right.
The Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2012 (Punjab): Implements Article 25-A in Punjab, ensuring free education for children aged 5-16 years.
The Sindh Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2013: Implements the right to education in Sindh province.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Free Compulsory Primary and Secondary Education Act, 2017: Ensures free and compulsory education in KPK province.
The Balochistan Compulsory Education Act, 2014: Provides for compulsory education in Balochistan province.
The Punjab Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2014: Additional legislation in Punjab for free and compulsory education.
The Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2002: Establishes the Higher Education Commission to regulate and promote higher education in Pakistan.
The Universities Act (various): Different acts govern universities in different provinces, ensuring quality higher education.
The Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2001: Regulates private educational institutions to ensure quality and prevent exploitation.
The National Education Policy: Various iterations provide framework for education policy, including gender equality in education.
The Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010: Applies to educational institutions, protecting students and staff from harassment.
The Punjab Educational Endowment Fund Act, 2014: Provides scholarships and financial assistance for education, particularly for underprivileged students.
The Sindh Education Foundation Act, 1992: Establishes foundation to promote education, especially for girls and marginalized communities.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Education Foundation Act, 2011: Promotes education through various programs and scholarships.
The Balochistan Education Endowment Fund Act, 2014: Provides educational scholarships and support in Balochistan.
The National Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2012: Monitors and promotes women's education and gender equality in educational institutions.
The Prevention of Anti-Women Practices (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2011: Prohibits practices that prevent women from accessing education.
The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929: By preventing child marriage, indirectly supports girls' right to education.
The Employment of Children Act, 1991: Prohibits child labor, ensuring children can attend school instead of working.
The Constitution of Pakistan, Article 34: Directs the state to take steps to ensure full participation of women in all spheres of national life, including education.
